summary: Session.Save must write through a unique temp file under cliutil.WithFileLock, and Shop must capture raw Set-Cookie headers (via an http.RoundTripper wrapper) so a renewed KEYCLOAK_IDENTITY's extended expiry is persisted, because cookiejar.Jar exposes cookie values but never expiry.
reason: Two concurrent CLI invocations saving session.json at once could interleave a torn write or race the rename since both used the same fixed '.tmp' name with no locking; separately, MergeFromJar only ever saw cookie values (the jar has no exported way to read back a stored cookie's expiry), so a renewed single-sign-on cookie kept its original expiry and users needed another browser login despite renewing regularly.
validated_outcome: go test ./internal/rewe/... passes with the existing TestSessionCookies/TestSessionSaveLoadAndPath coverage plus the transport-level cookie capture wired into OpenWith/NewShopWithClient.
